parsed.explanation: The national framework imposes tier-1 universal exposures: passport sex-marker rules force birth-sex documents on visitors, X markers are blocked, entry officers are directed to refuse cases with 'reasonable doubt' about sex and can pursue lifetime fraud findings, and multiple foreign governments issued trans-specific travel advisories after detentions of foreign nationals over visa issues. Facility bans and criminal-trespass exposure apply in many states (documented arrest), and custody/immigration detention show severe documented abuse. These are efficient institutions enforcing hostile rules — no working remedy, litigation unresolved — placing the parent well below the reduced-risk band despite no presentation offence and partial equality protections. The division itself is among the most protective: shield laws, comprehensive care coverage, refuge protections, and no documented local facility ban, warranting a position above the parent average; but rule 12 bars the local tolerance from neutralising the national passport, entry, national-facility and national-custody regime every visitor passes through, and a documented local hostile layer (birth-sex prison housing used as punishment) also weighs. Documented protective local machinery modestly offsets but cannot cancel the national layer: 0.42.
